30 An electron passes into the space between two parallel plates that are 5.0 cm apart and which
are maintained at electric potentials of +2000 V and –500 V, respectively.
+2000 V
electron
5.0 cm
–500 V
What is the electric force on the electron?
A
1.6 × 10–15
N
B
4.8 × 10–15
N
C
6.4 × 10–15
N
D
8.0 × 10–15
N

hints: Notice the two plates are at $+2000 \text{ V}$ and $-500 \text{ V}$ with separation $5.0 \text{ cm}$ - the field depends on the change in potential from one plate to the other.
Recall that for parallel plates the uniform field is $E = V/d$, where $V$ is the full potential difference and $d$ must be in metres.
Then use $F = qE$ for the electron with charge magnitude $1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and check the power of ten for the force in $\text{N}$.
walkthrough: Identify the potential difference between the plates: $V = (+2000) - (-500) = 2500 \text{ V}$, not $2000 \text{ V}$ or $500 \text{ V}$ alone.
Convert separation to SI units: $d = 5.0 \text{ cm} = 0.050 \text{ m}$.
Calculate the uniform electric field strength: $E = V/d = 2500/0.050 = 5.0 \times 10^{4} \text{ V m}^{-1}$.
Use $F = qE$ with electron charge magnitude $q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$: $F = (1.6 \times 10^{-19}) \times (5.0 \times 10^{4})$.
Evaluate: $F = 8.0 \times 10^{-15} \text{ N}$, directed toward the positive plate. This is option D.

A.explanation: Gives $1.6 \times 10^{-15} \text{ N}$, which is the force for only $500 \text{ V}$ across $5.0 \text{ cm}$, ignoring the $+2000 \text{ V}$ plate.

B.explanation: Gives $4.8 \times 10^{-15} \text{ N}$, which corresponds to $1500 \text{ V}$, found by wrongly doing $2000 - 500$ instead of $2000 - (-500)$.

C.explanation: Gives $6.4 \times 10^{-15} \text{ N}$, which is the force for only $2000 \text{ V}$ across $5.0 \text{ cm}$, ignoring the $-500 \text{ V}$ plate.

D.explanation: Uses the full $2500 \text{ V}$ potential difference to give $E = 5.0 \times 10^{4} \text{ V m}^{-1}$ and $F = eE = 8.0 \times 10^{-15} \text{ N}$.
